requirements.note: Newest-first feed with avatar, author, handle, relative time, full text, full-width rounded images at their own aspect ratio, and paging carousels with titles. Carousel cards are sloppy, though: portrait or square images are letterboxed on a grey card, cards in one row have different heights (232 vs 185 pt), and the title position moves between cards.
The heart fills red and the count goes up or down; a reply count is shown.

Tapping the text pushes a Post screen with a slightly larger image (386 vs 362 pt), a timestamp and a filler 'A moment shared with everyone.' line. Images and carousel cards open on black full screen; swipe down or X dismisses.
Pull to refresh adds three made-up posts (some with images) at the top, and the post count updates to 403.
Compose button opens a sheet with avatar, placeholder and auto-focused keyboard; Post is disabled when empty; the new post appears at the top.
Likes, the refreshed posts and the composed post all survived relaunch; relative times keep advancing (2m, 3m).

bugs: Carousel cards in the same row have different heights, and non-landscape images are letterboxed with grey bars instead of filling the card.
tells: No large navigation title: a small inline 'Feed' plus a custom serif 'A little closer.' header with a tracked 'THE LATEST' label reads as a designed web or landing page, not an iOS list.
Decorative layers icon in a glass circle at top left that looks like a button but does nothing.
Avatar initials, the share-style arrow and the header icons do not scale with Dynamic Type while the text grows very large.
Carousel card styling (grey letterbox background, mismatched heights) looks hand-built.
Detail screen padding text 'A moment shared with everyone.' is filler.
A.scroll: Slow drags and flings are smooth with no blank or popping rows. Flinging back to the top and pulling past it rubber-bands normally, and scroll position is kept after a push and pop.

requirements.note: Newest-first feed with author, handle, relative time, full text, full-width rounded images at their own aspect ratio, and carousels of uniform cropped rounded cards with titles below. There are no avatars, but the spec does not ask for them.
The heart fills pink-red and the count changes; a reply count is shown. VoiceOver reads the like as a switch, which is semantically odd but works.
Tapping the text or the chevron pushes a Post screen with an edge-to-edge (larger) image. Images and cards open on black full screen; swipe down or X dismisses.
Pull to refresh adds three made-up text posts at the top.
Compose sheet with a placeholder and auto-focused keyboard; Post is disabled when empty; the new post appears at the top.
Likes, the refreshed posts and the composed post all survived relaunch.

bugs: Relative time for new and refreshed posts stays at 'Just now' minutes later and after a relaunch; it never advances.
In dark mode the disabled Post button in compose does not look dimmed.
tells: A blue chevron button sits in each post's action row as the 'open post' affordance, which is odd for a feed; at the largest text size it wraps onto its own line.
No avatars, so posts look a bit bare compared with a typical iOS social app.
The like control is exposed as a Switch rather than a button.
The full-screen image is not exposed as an accessibility element.
B.scroll: Smooth slow drags and flings with no blank rows or popping images. The large title collapses into an inline title as a native navigation bar should, the bar blurs content scrolling under it, and scroll position is kept after returning from a post.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, including persistence. B looks like a standard iOS app: a large title that collapses, plain separated rows and uniform carousel cards. A wraps the feed in a custom editorial header with an inline title, and its carousel cards are uneven and letterboxed. A has nicer touches (avatars, refreshed posts with images, times that update), but B's frozen 'Just now' and odd chevron cost less than A's web-like look and carousel flaws.
